title: Low degree junta polynomial hypothesis
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $P\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let the failure parameter lie in $(0,1/2]$. Given a batch of the prescribed restricted sample size, consisting of a free-coordinate sign assignment and a label for each sample, apply the low-degree polynomial learner to the prescribed polynomial-learning portion of the batch. The result is an $\mathbb{F}_2$-coefficient hypothesis on the free-coordinate space, with degree bound $k-\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite set of coordinates in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
batch is indexed by the prescribed restricted sample count and contains a free-coordinate assignment and sign label
caveat: The formal statement delegates to learner and sample-construction definitions not included in the supplied definition descriptions, so the precise batch processing is only partially specified.
